_comment: HOSTING: all four archives are now served from the realm's own VPS at http://152.53.115.249/patches/ instead of GitHub releases. URLs are IMMUTABLE and carry the version in the filename -- the bytes behind a URL never change, so a player who started a download an hour ago can resume it safely, and rolling back is repointing at the previous filename (which is still on disk). The path field is what lands in the client and never carries a version: load order depends only on the archive letter. To publish a new version see PUBLISHING-PATCHES.md.
_comment2: MIRRORS: M and N are Trimitor's work and are NOT forked -- these are byte-identical copies of his release assets, still pinned to his tags, served from our host so that a deleted release or a dead repo cannot break new installs. The upstream each one came from is recorded in /srv/uncapped-patches/mirrors.tsv on the VPS, and a daily systemd timer (uncapped-mirror-check) reports when upstream ships a newer release carrying the same asset, or replaces the asset behind our pinned tag. Re-mirroring is always a deliberate act.

Mount pack: mount models backported from Cata 4.3.4 + MoP 5.4.8 into 3.3.5a (1353 displays / 183 new models), plus CreatureModelData.dbc and CreatureDisplayInfo.dbc. 298 MB and effectively static. Deliberately NOT folded into the consolidated DBC bundle: merging them would mean re-uploading and re-downloading 298 MB for every one-line DBC tweak. Keeping it separate costs one extra manifest entry and saves that every single release.

Verified by hashing the effective post-load-order view of the whole patch stack before and after: 5756 reachable entries both sides, 0 lost, 0 changed, all 12 DBCs byte-identical.
_letter: U, not R. It has to sort after every archive it replaces -- and -S sorted AFTER -R. Reusing R would mean a client that had not yet pruned its old -S would load S's LightFloatBand.dbc over the consolidated one. Identical bytes today, so it would look fine; the day we change the fog it would silently serve the old fog instead. A letter past S cannot have that problem. V-Z stay free for a hotfix archive that needs to override this one.

_history4: 2026-08.08a: Spell.dbc ONLY -- the HASTE tooltips now say CRIT DAMAGE. Haste is repurposed on this realm (SpellAuraEffects.cpp [Haste->CritDamage]): positive haste on a PLAYER is diverted into the crit-damage multiplier and no longer touches swing/cast/GCD speed, 1:1 in percentage terms. Every haste tooltip therefore described a mechanic that does not exist here -- report #259 (Warrior Flurry) is the visible half. 126 spells / 171 Description+ToolTip fields relabelled, selected by AURA TYPE (the ten types the diverting handlers serve: 9, 65, 138, 140, 141, 192, 193, 216, 218, 252) intersected with player reachability (SkillLineAbility + Talent + SpellItemEnchantment + item_template.spellid_*, closed over EffectTriggerSpell), then extended by hand with the talent/glyph/summon rows whose TEXT quotes one of those auras ($8515s1% melee haste). ⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED, and each for a reason that is about the code not the wording: negative amounts (Thunder Clap, Curse of Tongues, Icy Touch, Frost Fever, Hurricane) still slow exactly as written; PET haste (Cobra Reflexes, Frenzy, Ghoul Frenzy) is real because a pet is a Creature and the IsPlayer() guard fails; creature enrages likewise; amounts >= 1000 hit SetInstantCast and return BEFORE the diversion; and haste RATING is diverted at a DIFFERENT rate (1000 rating = +1% crit damage, in Player::ApplyRatingMod), so hundreds of item/enchant/food tooltips still say 'haste rating' and need a separate decision. Strings were APPENDED and the row's field repointed -- never edited in place, because one copy of 'Attack speed increased by $s1%.' is shared by Flurry and a hundred mob enrages. Built by ADDING Spell.dbc to 08.07a, never repacked. verify-stack with M= and N= in BOTH stacks: 5757 reachable both sides, 0 lost, 0 newly reachable, exactly 1 file changed (Spell.dbc) which is the intent; the other 12 DBCs byte-identical; fabricated filenames correctly absent. Script: Server/azerothcore-wotlk/tools/dbc/patch_spell_haste_to_critdamage.py. NOTE the archive grew 11.4MB -> 16.0MB: replacing an entry does not reclaim the old block, and the published 08.07a already carried ~8MB of dead space from earlier replacements. Content is correct either way; compacting is a separate, deliberate change.
_history5: 2026-08.08b: SkillLineAbility.dbc ADDED (new to this archive) -- all 565 backported custom mounts now appear in the Mounts tab. The 3.3.5a client does NOT read a spell's effects to decide it is a mount; it reads SkillLineAbility.dbc and asks whether the spell is reachable on SkillLine 777 ('Mounts'). Our 565 mounts (spells 850000-850564, items 90000-90564, taught by lua_scripts/mount_items.lua) shipped in Spell.dbc with NO SkillLineAbility row at all, so every one of them has always been spellbook-only and invisible in the Mounts tab. Report #151 is one symptom, not the bug: the STARTER mount 850139 'Mastiff (Dog Red)' (lua_scripts/starter_mount.lua, 167 characters) is simply the one of the 565 everybody owns. Measured on the live file before writing: 565/565 present in Spell.dbc, 565/565 carrying the mount auras, 0/565 with any SkillLineAbility row. 'These are mounts' is a measurement, not an assumption -- their effect/aura shapes are exactly Blizzard's two: effect=(6,6,0) aura=(78,32,0) x345 ground, same as spell 458 Brown Horse, and effect=(6,6,6) aura=(78,207,32) x220 flying, same as 32235. BASE COPY: stock patch-enUS-3.MPQ, which is the archive that WINS load order for this file -- locale-enUS, patch-enUS and patch-enUS-2 each carry an older copy, and none of M/N/Q/U had it; the stock archive was proven byte-identical (sha256 d61a60297af9044d926754d997cd5aa630500cd003d41983a9ccb5b324d61299) to the one in the live client. THE ROWS: 565 appended, IDs 21981..22545 (straight after the file's existing max of 21980 -- contiguous on purpose, since reusing the spell ids as row ids would inflate the client's id-indexed span forty-fold), SkillLine 777, everything else zero except MinSkillLineRank=1, which is the shape 309 of the 315 existing 777 rows already use. The 10219 pre-existing records are byte-identical and in the same order, and the string block is unchanged. SERVER UNTOUCHED: this is a client-classification file; the worldserver's own SkillLineAbility.dbc gates nothing here (the mounts are learned via Eluna Player:LearnSpell, not skill rewards), so no rebuild and no restart. Built by ADDING to 08.08a via StormLib, never repacked. verify-stack with M= and N= in BOTH stacks: 5757 -> 5758 reachable, 0 lost, 0 CHANGED bytes, exactly 1 newly reachable (skilllineability.dbc) which is the intent, other 12 DBCs byte-identical, PASS. Negative controls: fabricated filenames (SkillLineAbilities.dbc, MountCapability.dbc, NoSuchFile.dbc) correctly absent; rows for Fireball 133, Brown Horse 458, Blacksmithing 2018 and Apprentice Riding 33388 identical to stock; spells 849999/850565/900139 correctly have no row. Script: Server/azerothcore-wotlk/tools/dbc/patch_skilllineability_custom_mounts.py.
_history6: 2026-08.08c: Spell.dbc -- the SAME 565 custom mounts can now be cast while moving. Cast-while-moving is a shipped realm feature with two halves that have to agree. The SERVER half (src/server/scripts/Custom/cast_while_moving.cpp:101) strips SPELL_INTERRUPT_FLAG_MOVEMENT (0x01, SpellDefines.h:26) from every cast-time spell at startup and the live log confirms it runs: 'Cast while moving: cleared movement interrupt on 13936 cast-time spell(s)'. The CLIENT half is this Spell.dbc, and it has to carry the same stripped flags because the client refuses the cast locally and never sends a packet -- which is why no server change could ever reach this. The 565 custom mount rows were authored separately and never went through the stripping pass. Report #292 ('you cannot mount the starter dog mount while moving, like every other mount') is the visible half via starter mount 850139. MEASURED, and this doubles as the proof that field 31 is InterruptFlags since no other field gives this answer: spells game-wide still carrying 0x01 = 565, and they are EXACTLY ids 850000-850564, with 0 anywhere else in the game. DISTRIBUTION: all 565 read 31 (0x1F) uniformly -- MOVEMENT|PUSH_BACK|INTERRUPT|AUTOATTACK|DAMAGE -- and all 565 become 30 (0x1E). The bit was MASKED OFF, not assigned: assigning 30 happens to agree today, but the other four bits are real and had to survive, and a future row that read something other than 31 would have been silently flattened. 30 is exactly what stock Brown Horse (458) and Golden Gryphon (32235) carry, so the 565 end up flag-identical to real Blizzard mounts rather than to a value we invented. BLAST RADIUS, measured by diffing the record block against 08.08b: 565 differing bytes, 565 rows, ONE distinct field touched (31), spell ids touched == exactly 850000..850564, string block byte-identical, record/field counts unchanged. Game-wide carriers of 0x01 afterwards: 0. Negative controls: Fireball 133, Heal 2054, Shadow Bolt 686, Wrath 5176 all keep 14 (0x0E) unchanged; Brown Horse 458 and Golden Gryphon 32235 keep 30; custom-but-not-a-mount Mending Fatigue 850565 keeps 0; fabricated filenames absent. Built by ADDING to 08.08b, never repacked -- the 08.08b SkillLineAbility.dbc survives byte-identical (sha256 3d3cd188589666a0..., all 565 SkillLine-777 rows still readable out of 08.08c). verify-stack with M= and N= in BOTH stacks, 08.08b -> 08.08c: 5758 reachable both sides, 0 lost, 0 newly reachable, exactly 1 file CHANGED (Spell.dbc) which is the intent, other 13 DBCs byte-identical including skilllineability.dbc. Cumulative published-08.08a -> 08.08c: 0 lost, 1 newly reachable (skilllineability.dbc), 1 changed (spell.dbc) -- exactly the two intended changes and nothing else. ⚠ verify-stack exits 1 on ANY byte change by design, so a Spell.dbc edit always reports FAIL; the check that matters is that the CHANGED list is exactly what you meant, same as 08.08a. NOTE the archive grew 16.1MB -> 20.6MB: replacing the 49.5MB Spell.dbc does not reclaim its old block. Content is correct; compacting stays a separate, deliberate change. Script: Server/azerothcore-wotlk/tools/dbc/patch_spell_custom_mount_cast_while_moving.py.

_comment: THE PATCHED CLIENT EXECUTABLE. Stock 3.3.5a 12340 with LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE set and an import-table entry for UncappedCT.dll, which is what gets our code loaded before the client's entry point runs. Shipped whole rather than patched on the player's machine: every install then runs a byte-identical binary we can verify by hash, instead of the output of patch logic running on 40 different machines. The path is the RENAMED name the launcher's client hardening uses -- ClientHardening deletes a stock Wow.exe when this file is present, so the install ends up with exactly one runnable client.
_note: Not in payload/ and never committed: it is a modified Blizzard binary, and the payload tree is a public git repo.

_comment: THE INJECTED RUNTIME. A HARD dependency of the executable above -- import injection means the loader resolves it before any game code runs, so if this file is missing the client does not start at all (exit 0xC0000135, STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND). The launcher checks for it before every launch and tells the player to add an antivirus exclusion, because a real-time scanner quarantining it AFTER the sync verified it is the realistic way it goes missing. Built /MT so KERNEL32 is its only import: a 3.3.5a install has no reason to have a VC redistributable.
_note: Must stay in step with the executable above: they share the wire-magnitude codec and the native-channel frame format. Publish them together, always.
